correctness.rationale: With λ=α+2, the probability-normalized Bergman kernel is (1−z·conj(w))^(−λ). In the weighted R R* kernel the Jacobian factors of x=tanh(u) turn each endpoint factor into sech^λ; 1−tanh(u)tanh(v)=cosh(u−v)/(cosh(u)cosh(v)) leaves exactly sech^λ(u−v). This also proves boundedness without assuming it: on compactly supported chord tests the kernel computes the squared norm of the adjoint, bounded by the L¹ convolution norm. The range of R is dense since orthogonality to weighted polynomials implies a function times the bounded, positive-a.e. weight is orthogonal to all polynomials; R is injective by analyticity. Thus the one-diameter Gram operator is unitarily equivalent to the positive beta-integral multiplier. Its essential range is [0,Cα] and every subspace above a strict lower cutoff below Cα is infinite-dimensional. When θ∈(0,π), the cross-kernel denominator is bounded away from zero and the endpoint factors give a Hilbert–Schmidt operator. The positive Calkin images multiply to zero, so the spectrum of their sum is the union of the bands. The unit constant test gives Dα=2∫sech^(2λ)(u) du, strictly between Cα and 2Cα by the stated pointwise cosh comparison. Hence the spectral top is isolated with finite multiplicity. At coincidence the sum is 2Q; strong rotation continuity is uniform on each fixed finite-dimensional test space, so min–max gives arbitrarily many eigenvalues above each fixed μ in the claimed gap for all sufficiently small θ. For each fixed distinct angle there is no accumulation on the compact interval [μ,2Cα] outside the essential spectrum. The triangle bound and strong limit give the norm limit. The beta/gamma checker is only a diagnostic and was read, not executed. The verification sentence calling integrability exact in α>−1 should be read within the Bergman regime: integrability of that squared weight alone in fact needs only α>−2. This does not alter the proof or any claimed range.

value.rationale: A natural pair of traces changes from compactly coupled channels to identical channels as the angle closes. The theorem gives the exact essential edge on both sides and the mechanism by which a divergent number of discrete eigenvalues can coexist with a stable noncoincident essential edge and convergent ordinary norm. This supplies information not captured by a two-trace inequality or a single-angle bound.
